dangerous_functions.LOAD_FILE: Reads arbitrary files from the database server's filesystem.
dangerous_functions.SLEEP: Deliberately stalls execution — used for time-based blind SQL injection or denial-of-service.
dangerous_functions.BENCHMARK: Forces expensive repeated computation — a denial-of-service vector.
dangerous_functions.GET_LOCK: Acquires a named lock, which can stall other database connections.
dangerous_functions.RELEASE_LOCK: Releases a named lock; paired with GET_LOCK-based abuse.
dangerous_functions.INTO_OUTFILE: Writes query results out to a file on the server's filesystem (structural clause, also checked directly).
dangerous_functions.INTO_DUMPFILE: Writes a single row/blob to a file on the server's filesystem (structural clause, also checked directly).
dangerous_functions.EXTRACTVALUE: XML function abused for error-based injection — a malformed XPath echoes query results inside the error message.
dangerous_functions.UPDATEXML: XML function abused for error-based injection — a malformed XPath echoes query results inside the error message.
dangerous_functions.NAME_CONST: Used in error-based injection to force duplicate-column errors that leak values.
dangerous_functions.SYS_EXEC: Common malicious user-defined function (lib_mysqludf_sys) that runs operating-system commands.
dangerous_functions.SYS_EVAL: Common malicious user-defined function (lib_mysqludf_sys) that runs OS commands and returns their output.

system_info_functions.USER: Reveals the connected database user — used for reconnaissance/fingerprinting.
system_info_functions.CURRENT_USER: Reveals the effective database user and host — used for reconnaissance.
system_info_functions.VERSION: Reveals the database server version — used to target version-specific exploits.
system_info_functions.DATABASE: Reveals the name of the current database — used for reconnaissance.
system_info_functions.SCHEMA: MySQL synonym for DATABASE() — reveals the current database name.
system_info_functions.SESSION_USER: Reveals the session's authenticated user — used for reconnaissance.
system_info_functions.SYSTEM_USER: Synonym for USER() — reveals the connected database user.
system_info_functions.CONNECTION_ID: Reveals the server connection/thread id — used for reconnaissance.
